assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and molecular sieves with defined pore architectures and active sites underlies petrochemical refining, emissions control and fine-chemical catalysis at huge industrial scale. The work links structure-directing agents, new framework topologies and site engineering to catalytic function, and it is close to my own structural field, where structure solution of nanocrystalline zeolites by electron diffraction has enabled much of this design.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalyst design, many framework and active-site concepts), Davis (structure-directing agent and framework synthesis, templated catalysts) and Zones (organic SDA design, Chevron commercial zeolites such as SSZ-13) are decisive and complementary. Jihong Yu and Tsapatsis are also strong, so the three-way choice is a judgment, and credit is split between synthesis, catalysis and industrial application.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and deployment; the field is mature and the recognition is timely, with no risk of premature judgment. Porous frameworks were recently honored in another form, which could make the committee hesitate over a closely related area.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views zeolite design as sufficiently distinct from the recently recognized framework-materials prize.
Which three of the five credited people are most decisive; my selection is partly subjective.
I did not verify industrial attribution details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis created a general platform for radical and single-electron-transfer reactions under mild conditions, widely used in medicinal chemistry, late-stage functionalization and materials synthesis. It is conceptually clear and has had enormous practical reach.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and Nicewicz independently introduced the synthetic uses of visible-light photocatalysis around 2008-2012; MacMillan and Fukuzumi, König and Melchiorre also contributed. MacMillan already shared a prize for organocatalysis, so I propose the three others, but the allocation is contentious and four to seven people are credited.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with broad independent adoption in academia and industry. Timing is good, though overlap with earlier prizes for catalysis and cross-coupling is a consideration.
uncertainties: Priority disputes with earlier photochemical precedents (Fukuzumi, Kellogg, Cano-Yelo and Deronzier).
Prior prize to one key contributor complicates a fair configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one base into another without double-strand breaks, a chemistry-driven advance in genome editing combining protein engineering, directed evolution and nucleoside deaminase chemistry, with clinical translation already underway.
assessment.attribution: David R. Liu led the invention; Alexis Komor and Nicole Gaudelli were the lead researchers on the cytosine and adenine base editors respectively. Akihiko Kondo and Keiji Nishida's independent deaminase-based editing is a distinct line. A single-laureate configuration for Liu is plausible, with prime editing as a related contribution.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly validated across many labs and in clinical trials, though long-term clinical evidence is still accumulating. Recent genome-editing recognition (CRISPR) is adjacent.
uncertainties: Whether the work is judged chemistry rather than biology or medicine.
Whether base editing and prime editing should be one recognition.
Clinical durability and safety are still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity through PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new pharmacological modality that targets previously undruggable proteins by hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system. It is a conceptual change in how drugs are designed, with many compounds in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the first PROTACs; Ciulli provided structure-guided design and VHL ligands; Handa, Ito and others uncovered cereblon as the thalidomide target. The credit list is long and a clean three-person set is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Strong mechanistic evidence and rapid adoption, but approval of degrader drugs is still pending, so the clinical vindication is incomplete.
uncertainties: Premature if clinical validation is required.
Competing claim of the molecular-glue and cereblon strand (Handa, Ito).
Number of credited contributors exceeds three.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structure determination from nano- and microcrystals and time-resolved studies before radiation damage. It relates directly to my interest in structure determination from very small crystals and has opened ultrafast structural chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the 2011 proof-of-principle with Fromme, Hajdu, Schlichting and many collaborators; the credit is distributed across large collaborations and facility builders. Chapman, Fromme and Schlichting is a reasonable but debatable subset, as Hajdu is also a founding figure.
assessment.maturity: Methodology now well established at several XFELs with many independent structures, though impact on chemistry is concentrated at a few large facilities. Competing recognition for cryo-EM and microED limits novelty relative to alternatives.
uncertainties: Facility dependence and the large team nature of the discovery.
Uncertainty about Hajdu's status and contribution relative to the others.
Whether it is considered chemistry rather than physics or biology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced an extraordinary rise in solar-cell efficiency within a decade, with a rich solid-state chemistry of composition, defects and crystal structure. The scientific impact and the pace of change are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cells; Park developed the solid-state cell with improved efficiency; Snaith's meso-superstructured and planar devices drove the field, with Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also important. Credit is complex.
assessment.maturity: Rapid performance progress but stability, lead toxicity and scale-up are unresolved, which makes it arguably premature for a prize.
uncertainties: Long-term stability and commercial viability are unproven.
Contested attribution among many strong contributors.
I did not verify the details of the first-device chronology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atomic-resolution nc-AFM with CO-functionalized tips shows the bond structure of individual molecules and allows identification of reaction products on surfaces, a direct, visual chemical result with value for on-surface synthesis and structure elucidation.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl developed the qPlus sensor and frequency-modulation atomic resolution; Gross and Meyer at IBM Zurich demonstrated intramolecular bond imaging with CO tips in 2009. Eigler and Ho contributed to scanning-probe manipulation and spectroscopy, but are more central to a separate earlier achievement.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in many laboratories and well understood, though applications are mostly limited to model surface systems.
uncertainties: Breadth of impact beyond ultrahigh-vacuum model systems.
Relative standing of Eigler and Ho for a possible alternate configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas (M41S, MCM-41) opened a new class of crystalline-like solids with tunable mesopores of 2-50 nm, extending molecular-sieve chemistry to larger molecules and templating for nanostructured materials. Structural characterization of these materials relied heavily on electron microscopy and diffraction.
assessment.attribution: Kresge, Beck and colleagues at Mobil discovered M41S; Ryoo and Inagaki contributed independently and developed ordered mesoporous carbon and organosilica; Stucky and Zhao developed SBA-15 and other large-pore materials. Priority and credit between Mobil, Japanese and later groups are complicated.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely used, though its commercial impact is smaller than that of zeolites, so the prize case is somewhat weaker and perhaps less timely.
uncertainties: Industrial impact is more limited than that of microporous zeolites.
Mobil patent-era corporate authorship complicates individual credit.
Overlap with the zeolite candidate.
